public_rationale: The accessible research documents weak construction progress for many announced projects and identifies risks to delivery. It does not establish how much AI capacity actually missed deadlines due by August. Delays also appear uneven across developers. Forecast year-end shortfalls cannot be treated as completed failures, and the available records do not settle the claimed industry-wide pace.
limitations: Announced-project samples may overrepresent speculative developments.
Large absolute additions and substantial schedule delays can occur together.
General data-center capacity is not automatically AI IT capacity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center capacity is coming online very slowly.

statement.excerpt: Right now, capacity is coming on very, very slowly, and nobody really wants to talk about it.

from_speaker: capacity is coming on very, very slowly
our_interpretation: Capacity means energized and usable AI data-center IT capacity.
In context, the ordinary comparison is actual commissioning against announced delivery schedules and the scale of promised deployment.
Very slowly means substantial, widespread lag, not merely that some projects encounter delays.
I use January through August 2026: the current year's rollout through the latest completed calendar month before publication.
The accompanying remark about nobody wanting to discuss the issue is rhetorical and is not part of the supplied normalized capacity proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, comparable project records show substantial capacity-weighted commissioning shortfalls against schedules due by the target-period end.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, comparable records show operational AI capacity substantially meeting or exceeding schedules due during the target period, without widespread material delay.

evidence.excerpt: Around 11GW remains in the announced stage with no visible construction progress, despite typical build timelines of 12–18 months.
evidence.explanation: The research documents a gap between announcements and construction progress early in 2026. It covers large data centers and AI factories together, and its year-end delay forecast is not an observed AI commissioning shortfall through August.

evidence.excerpt: Delays appear to be most pronounced among smaller and newer entrants, Wang said.
evidence.locator: Paragraph following the discussion of QTS project transparency
evidence.explanation: The report's author describes uneven delays across developers. This cautions against treating the announced-project sample as a measure of the whole AI industry's commissioning rate.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A capacity-weighted ledger of AI projects with original delivery schedules and achieved operational IT MW through August 2026, including both timely and delayed projects.
